import pandas as pd

# File paths for source data
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_30/test_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_30/test_1.csv"

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Source0 schema: ['userId', 'movieId', 'tag', 'timestamp']
# Source1 schema: ['movieId', 'title', 'genres']

# Target schema: ['movieId': int, 'title': str, 'genres': str, 'userId': int, 'tag': str, 'timestamp': int]

# Step 1: Join source0 and source1 on 'movieId' to get all columns needed for the target
# source0 has userId, tag, timestamp
# source1 has movieId, title, genres
# Join on movieId (inner join to keep only matching movieIds)

merged = pd.merge(source0, source1, on='movieId', how='inner')

# Step 2: Ensure columns are in the target schema order and types are correct
# Target columns: movieId (int), title (str), genres (str), userId (int), tag (str), timestamp (int)

# Convert columns to correct types
merged['movieId'] = merged['movieId'].astype(int)
merged['title'] = merged['title'].astype(str)
merged['genres'] = merged['genres'].astype(str)
merged['userId'] = merged['userId'].astype(int)
merged['tag'] = merged['tag'].astype(str)
merged['timestamp'] = merged['timestamp'].astype(int)

# Reorder columns to match target schema
target_df = merged[['movieId', 'title', 'genres', 'userId', 'tag', 'timestamp']]

# Step 3: Write the result to the target CSV file
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_30/target_multisource_cot.csv"
target_df.to_csv(target_path, index=False)
